newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul confirms N.Korean peace briefing request.
newsitem.headline: Seoul confirms N.Korean peace briefing request.

text.p: North Korea has asked for a second briefing with South Korea and the United States on proposed peace talks, Seoul's foreign ministry spokesman said on Monday.

But the spokesman declined to comment on domestic media reports that Pyongyang had called the session to give an answer on the proposal for four-nation peace talks made last year by U.S. President Bill Clinton and his South Korean counterpart Kim Young-sam.
The talks, which would also include China, are aimed at securing a lasting peace to replace an armistice that ended the 1950-53 Korean War.
"There is no reason for South Korea not to attend the briefing," said spokesman Lee Kyu-hyung.
"But we will have to consult the U.S. and China before our final decision."
Asked whether Pyongyang would deliver its formal response to the peace talks proposal, Lee said: "I can't say what will be said at the briefing."
Lee confirmed that Pyongyang officials had suggested the briefing at a working level meeting in New York with U.S. and South Korean representatives.
South Korean and U.S. officials briefed North Korean diplomats for the first time on March 5 in New York. There have been two subsequent working-level contacts, also in New York.

"I feel optimistic about the briefing, but it's hard to say which way it will go," said Song Young-shik, Deputy Foreign Minister for Political Affairs, who led the South Korean team at the first briefing.
